es: Examinar una publicación viral, contrastarla con dos fuentes y explicar a un amigo qué es fiable y qué no, con certeza graduada.

teaching.en: This viral post says that all schools will close for two weeks.
teaching.es: Esta publicación viral dice que todos los colegios cerrarán dos semanas.
teaching.explanationEs: Viral: se comparte muy deprisa. Que sea viral no la hace cierta.
segments: This viral post says that all
schools will close for two weeks.
teaching.audioText: This viral post says that all schools will close for two weeks.

teaching.en: The post has no source, and it tells you to share it quickly.
teaching.es: La publicación no tiene fuente y te dice que la compartas rápido.
teaching.explanationEs: Señales de sesgo: ninguna fuente y presión para compartir (share now).
segments: The post has no source, and it
tells you to share it quickly.
teaching.audioText: The post has no source, and it tells you to share it quickly.

teaching.en: A reliable source, like the school office, can verify the news.
teaching.es: Una fuente fiable, como la oficina del colegio, puede comprobar la noticia.
teaching.explanationEs: Reliable: se puede confiar en ella. Verify: comprobar si algo es cierto.
segments: A reliable source, like the school
teaching.audioText: A reliable source, like the school office, can verify the news.

teaching.en: The local radio says that only one school will close, so the post is probably a rumour.
teaching.es: La radio local dice que solo un colegio cerrará, así que la publicación probablemente es un rumor.
teaching.explanationEs: Rumour: noticia sin confirmar que circula entre la gente. Se contrasta con otra fuente.
segments: The local radio says that only one school will
close, so the post is probably a rumour.
teaching.audioText: The local radio says that only one school will close, so the post is probably a rumour.

teaching.en: The post uses urgent words like BREAKING to make you panic.
teaching.es: La publicación usa palabras urgentes como BREAKING para que te asustes.
teaching.explanationEs: Urgent: palabras de urgencia y mayúsculas son una señal de sesgo.
segments: The post uses urgent words like
teaching.audioText: The post uses urgent words like BREAKING to make you panic.

teaching.en: Given that two reliable sources disagree with the post, it is unlikely that the offer is real.
teaching.es: Dado que dos fuentes fiables contradicen la publicación, es poco probable que la oferta sea real.
teaching.explanationEs: Given that + dato, it is unlikely that…: conclusión con certeza graduada.
segments: Given that two reliable sources disagree with the post,
it is unlikely that the offer is real.
teaching.audioText: Given that two reliable sources disagree with the post, it is unlikely that the offer is real.

prompt.es: ¿Qué señal de sesgo tiene esta publicación?

choices.text: It gives the name of the company.
It includes a link to a report.
It pushes you to share it immediately.

feedback.es: SHARE NOW presiona para compartir deprisa, una señal de sesgo. No hay empresa ni informe a la vista.

hint.es: Busca lo que te presiona a actuar rápido.

origin.text: URGENT!!! Free phones for everyone! SHARE NOW before they delete this!

prompt.es: Completa: «La oficina de la ciudad es una fuente fiable de información.»

feedback.es: Reliable significa que se puede confiar en ella: una fuente oficial lo es.

origin.text: The city office is a ___ source of information.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La publicación no da fuente ni fecha.»

answer.text: The post gives no source and no date

feedback.es: Lo que falta (fuente y fecha) es una señal para desconfiar.

hint.es: Señala lo que falta en la publicación.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada elemento de una publicación con su papel al comprobarla.

feedback.es: BREAKING presiona, sin enlace ni nombre no hay fuente, la web oficial es una fuente y la radio es la segunda fuente contrastada.

choices.text: It is unlikely that the post is true.

feedback.es: Con dos fuentes en contra pero sin poder comprobarlo todo, lo prudente es it is unlikely that…

origin.text: Dos fuentes fiables contradicen la publicación, pero no puedes comprobarlo todo.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase que pida comprobarlo con otra fuente.

answer.text: Let's verify the news with the local radio.
accepted: Let's verify the news with the local radio.
We should verify the news with the local radio.
Let's check the news with the local radio.
Let us confirm the news with the local radio.

feedback.es: Let's + verbo base propone hacer algo juntos; verify señala que hay que comprobar con otra fuente.

origin.text: Dile a tu amigo que comprobéis la noticia con la radio local.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dice la fuente oficial.

choices.text: The museum gives tickets to everyone.
The museum is not giving away tickets.
The museum will close next week.

feedback.es: La web del museo niega la oferta: no regala entradas.

origin.audio: The post says that the museum gives free tickets to everyone who shares it. The museum website says that there is no such offer.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la mejor respuesta para explicar la conclusión a un amigo?

choices.text: I checked two sources, and the post is 100 per cent false, no doubt.
I checked nothing, but everybody shares it, so it is true.
I checked two sources, and they disagree with the post, so it may well be a rumour.

feedback.es: La respuesta que cita dos fuentes contrastadas y gradúa la certeza (may well) es la adecuada. Afirmar 100 % de certeza exagera, y no comprobar nada y fiarse de que todos la comparten no prueba nada.

origin.text: Has contrastado la publicación con dos fuentes que la contradicen.

prompt.es: Completa: «Muchos compartidos no demuestran que una publicación sea cierta.»

feedback.es: Prove = demostrar: compartir muchas veces no es una prueba.

origin.text: Many shares do not ___ that a post is true.

prompt.es: Explica a un amigo si fiarse de la publicación: sesgo, dos fuentes y conclusión graduada.

answer.text: Hi Sam, I do not think that post is reliable. First, it uses urgent words like URGENT and SHARE NOW, and it does not give a source. Second, I checked two sources. The shop website says that it is not giving away free bikes. The local radio says that there is only a ten per cent offer for students. Given that both sources disagree with the post, it is unlikely that the offer is real. It may well be a rumour, so please do not share it until we can verify it.
accepted: Hi Sam, I do not think that post is reliable. First, it uses urgent words like URGENT and SHARE NOW, and it does not give a source. Second, I checked two sources. The shop website says that it is not giving away free bikes. The local radio says that there is only a ten per cent offer for students. Given that both sources disagree with the post, it is unlikely that the offer is real. It may well be a rumour, so please do not share it until we can verify it.

Sam, I would not trust that post. It has no source, and words like URGENT and SHARE NOW try to make you act quickly. I checked the shop website, and it says that there is no offer of free bikes. The local radio only mentions a ten per cent offer for students. Because two reliable sources disagree with the post, it is probably a rumour. I cannot be completely sure, but I suggest that we wait and verify it before we share it.

feedback.es: La explicación a un amigo nombra señales de sesgo, contrasta dos fuentes y concluye con certeza graduada.

origin.text: Publicación: «URGENT! Free bikes for everyone! SHARE NOW before it is deleted!» Datos: la web de la tienda dice que no regala bicicletas; la radio local solo habla de una oferta del 10 % para estudiantes. Escribe a Sam unas 100 palabras.

choices.text: A post with no name and no link
A friend of a friend on a chat

feedback.es: La web oficial es una fuente fiable. Las otras dos no tienen nombre ni forma de comprobarse.

origin.text: Quieres saber si hay clase mañana y tienes tres lugares donde mirar.

answer.text: It may well be just a rumour
accepted: It may well be just a rumour
It may well just be a rumour

feedback.es: May well + verbo base expresa que es muy posible, sin ser seguro.

prompt.es: Completa: «Deberíamos comprobar la noticia con una segunda fuente.»

feedback.es: Verify (o check) indica que hay que comprobar el dato con otra fuente.

origin.text: We should ___ the news with a second source.
